content.title: About
content.content: Bread stuffing made with egg is a ready‑to‑eat product consisting of finely diced bread mixed with beaten eggs and seasonings. It is commonly used as a filling for pies, casseroles, and sandwiches. During preparation the bread absorbs the egg mixture, resulting in a soft, flavorful, and nutritious filling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally this stuffing was made at home to make use of leftover bread crumbs.
In some regions finely chopped onion or fresh herbs are added for extra aroma.
The combination of bread and egg provides a quick source of energy from carbohydrates and protein.
The stuffing can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 3 days and frozen for up to 2 months.
Variations may include cheese, ham, or vegetables.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Eggs provide a complete protein containing all essential amino acids, important for tissue repair.

items.title: Energy value
items.content: Carbohydrates from bread together with fats from eggs deliver sustained satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain vitamin B12, riboflavin and niacin, supporting metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The stuffing supplies iron, phosphorus and selenium, which are vital for blood formation and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Warm texture and soft consistency aid quick digestion.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: People allergic to eggs may experience reactions ranging from mild to anaphylactic after consumption.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: When salt is added, monitor the amount to stay within daily sodium recommendations.

items.title: Shelf life
items.content: Because of the eggs, the product spoils quickly if not stored properly; keep it refrigerated.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improper cooking of eggs can allow salmonella growth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use the stuffing as a filling for puff pastries, casseroles, sandwiches, or serve it as a hot side dish. Heat in the oven or on a skillet until golden before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for no more than 3 days. For longer storage freeze in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before consumption.
